record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: degree recovery by Fourier-magnitude summation processes
record.original_question: A summation process is a family sigma_{n,epsilon}, indexed by n in Z and 0 < epsilon < 1, with sup_n |n| |sigma_{n,epsilon}| < infinity for each epsilon and sigma_{n,epsilon} -> 1 as epsilon -> 0 for each fixed n. Given p > 3, does there exist a summation process depending only on p such that lim_{epsilon->0} sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} = deg f for every f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)? Similarly, given alpha <= 1/3, does such a process depending only on alpha exist for every f in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp., alpha <= 1/3), does there exist a summation process depending only on p (resp., alpha) such that (5.13) holds for every f?

artifact.category_tag: Fractional Sobolev maps and topological degree
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $f:S^1	o S^1$, write its Fourier expansion $f(	heta)\sim\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} a_n(f)\,e^{in	heta}$ with $a_n(f)= rac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(	heta)e^{-in	heta}\,d	heta$. For $f\in C^1(S^1;S^1)$ the (Brouwer) degree of $f$ equals $\deg f=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2$.

Define a \emph{summation process} to be a family $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\,0<\varepsilon<1}$ of real (or complex) numbers such that
(i) for each fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |n|\,|\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}|<\infty$, and
(ii) for each fixed $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}	o 1$ as $\varepsilon	o 0^+$.

For $p>1$, $s\in(0,1)$, let $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ denote the fractional Sobolev space of maps $S^1	o S^1$, and for $\alpha\in(0,1]$ let $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ denote the Hölder space.

Questions:
(a) Given $p>3$, does there exist a summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$ depending only on $p$ such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon	o 0^+}\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}=\deg f\qquad	ext{for every }f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)?$$
(b) Given $\alpha\le 1/3$, does there exist a summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$ depending only on $\alpha$ such that the same identity holds for every $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$?
artifact.status_search_result: No search result was found directly addressing this specific open problem on summation processes recovering the degree on $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for $p>3$ or on $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ for $\alpha\le 1/3$. It appears as an open problem in Brezis's list of favorite open problems and no subsequent resolution has been located.
